newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq lucky streak ends after 10-day ride.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq lucky streak ends after 10-day ride.

text.p: Nasdaq shares took a rest Thursday, snapping a 10-day string of record closes that matched the longest streak the index has seen in the 1990s.
The Nasdaq Composite Index slipped 11.78 points to 1568.85, losing 0.75 percent, with traders attributing most of the downturn to weakness in smaller technology companies.
Lehman Brothers trader Arun Kumar said he remained bullish on the sector, despite the shift in Nasdaq fortunes.
"Things don't go up in a straight line," Kumar said, adding he didn't see any overriding negative fundamentals at work Thursday.
Bucking the day's trend was Microsoft Corp whose shares closed up 1-1/16 in heavy trading as investors bet on the software giant's earnings, which were reported just after the close of trading.

Although it earned $0.80 a share, a penny above Wall Street forecasts and sharply above last year's earnings of $0.43, some investors were still disappointed. The stock fell slightly in after-hours trading.
Octel Communications Corp rose 3-3/8 to 30-1/8 on news it would be acquired by Lucent Technologies Inc.
